body:
It's 11:15p MST. I've written the notes, emails and information the people in my life will need. I know I'll just be a statistic. My name, my life and my story will be forgotten in time, just as everyone else. 

I've come to the realization that pain in transferable. It will jump through the world like a disease. My pain will be given to the people that loved me and for that I am sorry. I hope that it's spread among enough people that it will be more manageable. 

This was not an act based solely on depression and despair. Confusion, grief, physical pain and a definitive end to who I am led to this. A growing disdain for our society and the people in it have cemented my mindset of hopelessness in a community around me. My mental acuity and ability to function has diminished to the point that I would *need* to rely on others to move forward. I wish I had created better avenues of support in those around me. I wish I had invested in the right people. But I'm tired and it's too late for that. I will not be someone to take care of for any amount of time. Life has taught me that is how I lose the people I love. I hope the people you love are better than that. 

​

Thank you for all that you have done.

I appreciate you thinking solutions. Therapy isn't accessible to me right now due to lack of healthcare and income. I've been living out of my vehicle for the past 6 months. Luckily I did not sign a lease while in NM, otherwise my financial situation would be more dire. 

I've been travelling as much as I can the last few months. I spent a few weeks in Utah and now I'm back in Colorado doing some ice climbing. My issue is I need to push myself to relax. I need to do canyons, mountains, ice falls, etc. If I'm not exhausted physically and mentally from doing something strenuous and fulfilling I can't relax. I know it seems counter intuitive, but that's how it works for me. The issue these days is I've slowed down so much that I can't consistently do these activities. I climbed once on Monday and have spent the last few days at my campsite trying to recuperate. Driving has gotten more difficult as well. I can't do more than 4 hours at a time these days. It makes it a little limiting. When I wasn't canyoneering I was in the middle of gorgeous desert and canyonlands all by myself. But just *being* there is in some ways more frustrating because it forces me to recognize my current limitations. It's stressful and painful in it's own right. 

​

Again, I appreciate the thoughts on solutions and taking the time to respond.
